summary: The US strikes an Iranian island as Qatar reports progress, Russia hits Ukraine's grid before talks, US hiring surprises, Paraguay ousts its president, and COP31 opens.

question.text: Iran says tankers hit mines and US drones were shot down; the US says little or calls some reports invented. When the only sources for an event are the two sides fighting, what would you need to see before you believed either claim?

read.title: Russia's land gains in Ukraine dwindle as its diesel reportedly goes unsold
read.summary: Before the Abu Dhabi talks: how slowing Russian gains, Ukraine's strikes on refineries and Russia's fuel exports shape each side's bargaining power.

topics.heading: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Qatar reports progress in talks
topics.summary: President Trump confirmed what he called minor US strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first since the US election.[^1] A day later Qatar said its mediation had made significant progress, as oil ended its biggest weekly fall since 2022.[^2][^4]

lead.title: Trump confirms new US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island

alsoReported.title: Qatar says its mediation efforts between US and Iran continue to prevent escalation
Oil Posts Biggest Weekly Drop Since 2022

article: On Friday, Iranian state media reported two missile strikes on Qeshm, an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane that normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil. Trump confirmed them, describing a quick hit on an anti-aircraft system, and said of Iran: "They want to make a deal."[^1] Iranian media said its air defences shot down a US drone; the US military called the area "relatively calm" and gave no more detail.[^1]

At sea, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire on what they called unauthorised routes, and blamed the US for encouraging those ships to sail.[^3] No independent body has confirmed this, and Trump has accused Iran of inventing incidents.[^1] Iran has not shipped oil for export since mid-August because of the US naval blockade of its ports.[^3]

On Saturday, Qatar's prime minister said the US still wants a solution after the midterms and that "significant progress" has been made, adding that the goal is a good agreement, not a perfect one.[^2] Iran's plan, which Trump rejected in September, asks the US to lift the blockade, release frozen Iranian money and accept an Iranian-backed shipping route through Hormuz.[^2]

Markets are betting on calm. Brent crude, the global benchmark, settled near $98 a barrel on Friday after falling about 13% over the week, its biggest weekly drop since 2022, helped by Saudi and UAE exports returning to pre-war levels.[^4][^20] My read: small strikes alongside public talk of a deal look like pressure tactics on both sides. The thing to watch is whether direct US-Iran talks restart, or whether the larger US forces the New York Times reports are ready are used instead.[^1]
topics.differences: Iran says US drones were shot down and tankers were hit by mines; the US military gave few details, and Trump says Iran fabricates some incidents.[^1][^3] Iranian media earlier claimed five tankers and a tug were hit on Nov 5, which no maritime authority confirmed.[^1] Outlets put the oil drop for the week at about 12% to 13%.[^4][^20]

topics.heading: Russia strikes Ukraine's power grid three days before Abu Dhabi talks
topics.summary: Overnight, Russia fired 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles at Ukraine, hitting substations that link nuclear plants to Kyiv, Ukraine's president says.[^5] Moscow has named its team for US-Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11.[^7]

lead.title: Russia launches missile attack on Kyiv, injuring residents

alsoReported.title: Russia attacks substations linking Rivne, Khmelnytsky NPPs to Kyiv, central regions – Zelenskyy
Russia names delegation for Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine

article: President Zelensky says Russia's overnight attack used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, all of the missiles aimed at Kyiv and the region around it, with energy "once again the main target."[^5] Strikes hit substations that carry power from the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to the capital and central Ukraine, and power, water and heating in Kyiv were disrupted.[^5] Reported injuries rose during the day: Al Jazeera reported two people hurt, while Zelensky later said nine, including a child.[^6][^5]

The timing matters. The first three-way talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia since February are set for Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11.[^7] The Kremlin says its team will be led by Vladimir Medinsky and include two deputy foreign ministers and the head of military intelligence; Putin met them on Friday.[^7] Zelensky said Russia was "preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistic missiles" and asked for more US support and sanctions.[^5]

Ukraine is also striking Russia's energy. Al Jazeera, citing the Institute for the Study of War and Ukrainian figures, reports Ukraine hit eight Russian oil refineries in a week, and that Russia's gains on the battlefield have slowed sharply this year.[^19] Both sides seem to be trying to weaken the other's economy and strengthen their hand before negotiating.

What could happen next: earlier rounds in Abu Dhabi produced prisoner swaps but no ceasefire. My read is that a limited deal, such as a pause on energy strikes before winter, is more realistic than a full peace, because the two sides still disagree on territory and on who would guarantee any agreement.

topics.heading: Strong US jobs report raises odds of a December Fed rate hike
topics.summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than forecast, and unemployment fell to 4.1%.[^8] Traders now see about a 77% chance the Fed raises rates in December, and chip stocks bounced back after Thursday's crash.[^8][^10]

lead.title: October jobs report beats forecasts, lifting December Fed hike odds

alsoReported.title: Strong October jobs report sends yields higher
Wall Street rebounds as chip stocks rally after heavy AI-related selloff

article: The US Labor Department reported that employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against forecasts of roughly 59,000 to 65,000, and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%.[^8][^9] Earlier months were revised up, and average hourly pay rose 3.1% over the year.[^8]

Why it matters: the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, already raised rates in September and held them at 3.75% to 4% in October because inflation, pushed up by war-driven oil prices, is still above its 2% target.[^8] A strong job market gives it room to raise rates again. After the report, futures markets put the chance of a hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting at about 77%, and the yield on two-year US government bonds rose to about 4.5%.[^8][^9] Higher rates make mortgages, car loans and business borrowing more expensive.

Stocks steadied after Thursday's sell-off in AI and chip companies. On Friday the chip index rose about 4%, the Nasdaq about 1% and the S&P 500 slightly, though all major indexes were down for the week.[^10] Meanwhile the midterm count continued: Democrats had won 253 House seats to Republicans' 157 with 25 races uncalled, and hold 54 Senate seats with independents.[^11]

My read: the US economy looks stronger than many expected, which is good for workers but makes faster rate cuts less likely. Canada is in a different place, with unemployment rising, so the two central banks may move in different directions.

topics.heading: Paraguay removes President Peña after a major bank collapses
topics.summary: Paraguay's Congress impeached and removed President Santiago Peña after the failure of Ueno, a bank used by most of the country's adults.[^12] He is under house arrest, and Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in.[^12]

lead.title: Paraguay's Santiago Pena under arrest, new president Pedro Alliana sworn in

article: On Nov 3, Paraguay's central bank took over Ueno, the country's fifth-largest bank by deposits. AP reports it had about 3 million members, nearly two-thirds of adults, and held about $800 million in public money plus $355 million of state pension savings.[^12]

Peña offered to resign, but Congress refused and impeached him instead: the lower house voted 78-0 on Thursday and the Senate voted 44-0, with one abstention, to remove him on Friday.[^12] Prosecutors suspect him of breach of trust; he was a Ueno shareholder in 2023 and says he sold his shares in early 2025.[^12] At least 27 people have been charged, and there is an arrest warrant for the former central bank chief.[^12] Pedro Alliana, 52, became president.[^12]

Why it matters: when one bank holds the savings of most of a country, its failure becomes a political crisis, not only a financial one. Peña was a close ally of the US government in South America. What comes next depends on how much of people's money is recovered, and on whether the courts find he did anything wrong. Only one verified report was available, so details may change.

topics.heading: COP31 climate talks open Monday in Antalya with modest hopes
topics.summary: Nearly 200 countries meet in Antalya, Turkey, from Nov 9 to 20 for the UN climate summit.[^13] The hosts want a pledge to raise electricity's share of energy use, while the US government is staying out of the negotiations.[^13][^14]

lead.title: With temperatures rising, COP31 confronts familiar battles over cash and carbon

alsoReported.title: Daily Briefing: COP31 to start | Rosebank push | 'Simply staggering' El Niño
COP31 Antalya preview: seven issues to watch, November 9–20, 2026

article: COP31, the yearly UN climate conference, runs from Nov 9 to 20 in Antalya, with more than 100,000 people expected and world leaders speaking on Nov 11-12.[^13] Turkey hosts and holds the presidency, while Australia leads the negotiations under a compromise that settled a dispute over who would host.[^13][^15]

The hosts' main goal is a pledge to raise electricity's share of the world's final energy use from about 20% to 35% by 2035, since electric cars, heat pumps and factories can run on clean power.[^13][^14] African countries want a promise to triple money for adaptation, meaning help coping with heat, floods and drought.[^13] The US administration is not taking part in the talks, though some members of Congress will attend.[^13]

The gap is large. A UN tally of 154 national climate plans puts 2035 emissions only about 6% below 2019 levels, and the UN Environment Programme projects about 2.8°C of warming on current paths, far above the Paris goal of 1.5°C to well below 2°C.[^15] Fewer leaders are due to speak than at recent summits.[^15] A strong El Niño, a natural warming of the Pacific, may make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record.[^13][^14]

My read: expectations are low. A former French chief negotiator told AFP this "is not going to be the COP that changes the world."[^13] Smaller steps, like the electricity pledge or adaptation money, are the realistic test.
topics.differences: Carbon Brief describes Australia's Chris Bowen as president of the talks; AFP and others say Turkey's Murat Kurum is COP31 president and Bowen leads the negotiations.[^13][^14]

topics.heading: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated 'Critical' for hacking risk
topics.summary: OpenAI released a model that can find software flaws and help build working attacks, available only to vetted security customers.[^16] It is the first OpenAI model rated at the top level of its own cyber-risk scale.[^16][^17]

lead.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, and promises this one stays within 'rules of engagement'

alsoReported.title: Everything That Happened in AI Today (Friday, November 6, 2026)

article: OpenAI's new GPT-6 Cyber is built for security work: finding weaknesses in software before criminals do. The Register reports researchers used it to find 81 previously unknown serious flaws in the Firefox browser, which Mozilla is fixing, and to help build working exploits, meaning code that actually uses a flaw, for 948 Linux kernel weaknesses, 588 of them new.[^16]

OpenAI rated it "Critical", the highest cyber-risk level in its own safety framework, and is giving access only to selected security customers, widening over the coming weeks.[^16][^17] The company says it stayed within its permitted tasks more than 99% of the time; 0.07% of cases went out of bounds, and OpenAI did not describe them.[^16] It also raised its reward for people who report serious bugs in its own systems.[^16]

Why it matters: the same skill that helps defenders patch software could help attackers break into hospitals, power grids or banks. Companies argue it is safer for defenders to have these tools first. Critics worry that limits based on vetting customers are hard to enforce over time, and that a company is grading its own risk. Here my read is that both concerns are real.

What to watch: whether governments set rules for releasing such models, and whether other labs release similar tools. On the same day, the US Justice Department announced a task force to prosecute crimes that use advanced AI.[^17]

topics.heading: Nigerian court voids opposition candidate Atiku's 2027 nomination
topics.summary: A court in Nigeria set aside Atiku Abubakar's nomination as the main opposition party's presidential candidate for the January 2027 election.[^18] His party, the ADC, calls the ruling political and will appeal.[^18]

lead.title: Nigerian court voids candidacy of opposition ADC's Atiku for 2027 election

article: A single judge ruled that the African Democratic Congress (ADC) had not chosen its leaders at a proper national convention, and set aside both those leaders and Atiku's nomination, Reuters reports.[^18] The case was brought by a former deputy chair of the party.[^18]

Atiku, a former vice-president and the runner-up in the last election, was seen as President Bola Tinubu's strongest challenger; Tinubu has already launched his re-election campaign.[^18] The ADC's spokesman said "we have seen this script before" and the party will go to the Court of Appeal.[^18]

Why it matters: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and a sitting president there has lost only once, in 2015.[^18] Whether courts are seen as fair referees affects trust in the whole election. The ruling is not final, and the appeal could reverse it. Only one verified report was available.
topics.differences: The ADC says the ruling is politically motivated; the court's ruling rests on the party's internal rules for choosing leaders.[^18]
